strategic_capability_mapping.transition: The ledger payload contract registry becomes protocol-owned source-of-truth for event-specific schema versions, schema IDs, schema fingerprints, descriptor compatibility, and diagnostic instance fingerprints; brownie-store consumes it for append/read envelope validation while retaining v1 through v13 read/replay compatibility.
strategic_capability_mapping.why_now: After RRP-5.17 removed open payload families, release maintainability still risked global schema version churn, duplicate descriptor authority between brownie-store and brownie-protocol, and top-level-only strictness for nested object evidence.
strategic_capability_mapping.evidence: brownie-protocol::semantic_contract exposes ledger_payload_schema_version(kind), schema ID/fingerprint helpers, descriptor_for_version compatibility, and instance fingerprint helpers; brownie-store delegates schema authority to those helpers, writes event-specific current versions, accepts legacy v1 through v13 compatible envelopes on read only, and recursively bounds opaque nested object/array fields.
strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the post-RRP-5.17 ledger payload maintainability corrective while leaving runtime-release-guard-ci as the only Runtime-owned release blocker.

answers.strategic_capabilities: RRP-5.18 closes the ledger payload contract maintainability gap by moving schema version/ID/fingerprint/descriptor authority to brownie-protocol and making versions event-specific.
answers.new_capability: New ledger appends use each event kind current schema version, legacy global v13 envelopes remain read-only compatible, and nested opaque object/array payload fields are recursively bounded with forbidden raw-value key checks.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-5.17 closed open payload families but still had duplicated contract descriptors, a global LEDGER_PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_VERSION, and nested object fields that were only checked at the top level.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A single event payload change could churn every schema ID/fingerprint or diverge between store validation and protocol artifacts, and strict_typed payloads could still hide unbounded raw evidence inside nested objects.
answers.non_duplicative: This does not add another payload family slice; it consolidates the already-closed payload contract into one protocol-owned registry and preserves compatibility.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. No JSON-RPC method is added or broadened.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The generated contract and audit files are guard evidence only.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Ledger payload envelopes for new appends now use event-specific current versions; read/replay accepts compatible legacy v1 through v13 envelopes; bounded opaque nested fields reject overlarge or forbidden raw-value keys.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless/replay evidence remains typed while the schema registry can evolve per event without destabilizing unrelated ledger contracts.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the post-RRP-5.17 protocol/event maintainability corrective while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until runtime-release-guard-ci is directly hardened or owner-approved equivalent CI hardening exists.

brownie-store uses protocol helpers for ledger payload envelope creation and read validation.

accepted_capability: Rust protocol crate owns and generates the full explicit Runtime semantic protocol contract artifact.
The semantic contract includes recursive JSON Schema for all method param/result types, including nested structs/enums through $defs.
Durable ledger payload schema fingerprints are separate from diagnostic instance-shape fingerprints.
Every LedgerEventKind has an explicit payload schema classification and release-blocking status in generated evidence.
Every current LedgerEvent payload family now uses strict typed current schemas for new appends, except WorkspacePatchApprovalRequested which is payload_absent.
Open ledger payload families can no longer be treated as full typed payload schemas because release_blocking_open_payload_count is guarded at 0.
RRP-5.18 makes brownie-protocol the source registry for ledger payload schema versions, schema IDs, schema fingerprints, descriptors, and instance fingerprints.
New ledger appends use event-specific current schema versions while read/replay preserves compatible legacy v1 through v13 envelopes.
behavior_evidence: Rust semantic_contract tests cover generator freshness, canonical method-set equality, recursive nested schema refs, public-param unknown-field policy, and serde semantics.

brownie-store ledger_payload tests prove fixed schema versus instance fingerprint separation and reject empty, unknown-only, or malformed terminal, permission, selected tool, MCP approval, tool terminal, Codebase Index, verification recovery context, task/LLM lifecycle, task admission/mode-resolution, tool planning/intent parsing, subtask orchestration/dispatch, workspace patch, and headless payload fields before append.
